subsystems.name: Fermionic encoding
subsystems.role: maps the electrons (or lattice sites) onto qubits while preserving antisymmetry.
parts: local/compact encodings to cut gate count

subsystems.name: Trial-state preparation
subsystems.role: builds the approximate ground state that the Monte Carlo walk is biased towards.

subsystems.name: Projector and imaginary-time evolution
subsystems.role: the long imaginary-time projection that kills excited-state contributions.

subsystems.name: Sampling layer
subsystems.role: repeatedly measures the register in the basis needed to recover amplitudes and phases.

subsystems.name: Readout estimators
subsystems.role: turn hardware statistics into energies and correlation functions with controlled error.
parts: phase estimation or quantum signal processing

subsystems.name: Classical co-processor
subsystems.role: runs the conventional quantum Monte Carlo framework around the quantum samples.
parts: validation against exact diagonalisation, DMRG and diffusion Monte Carlo

subsystems.name: Error correction stack
subsystems.role: keeps long projector circuits coherent — required for the useful regime.
parts: surface or other quantum error-correcting code

buildSteps.title: Define the model and active space
buildSteps.detail: Choose the molecule or lattice, select the orbitals that carry the strong correlation, and write the Hamiltonian in second quantisation — the qubit cost scales with the number of spin-orbitals.

buildSteps.title: Map to qubits
buildSteps.detail: Apply a fermionic encoding so that creation and annihilation operators become qubit operations that respect antisymmetry, then compile the Hamiltonian into a weighted sum of Pauli strings.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the trial wavefunction
buildSteps.detail: Load a mean-field state or a variationally optimised circuit; its overlap with the true ground state controls how much imaginary-time projection is still needed.

buildSteps.title: Compile the projector
buildSteps.detail: Turn the imaginary-time (or projector) operator into block-encoded, controlled unitaries using qubitisation and linear combinations of unitaries, normalising the weights so the circuit is unitary.

buildSteps.title: Run the circuit and sample
buildSteps.detail: Execute the trial-state preparation and projector layers thousands of times on the processor, rotating the measurement basis to extract the off-diagonal amplitudes and signs the classical method cannot estimate.

buildSteps.title: Feed the samples into the classical estimator
buildSteps.detail: Use the measured ratios inside a classical quantum Monte Carlo loop — a Markov chain or reweighting step — so the sign problem is fixed by quantum data while the statistics stay on a classical machine.

buildSteps.title: Extract energies and observables
buildSteps.detail: Apply amplitude or phase estimation (or accumulate the classical estimator) to get ground-state energies and correlation functions with error falling polynomially in the number of shots rather than exponentially in system size.

buildSteps.title: Validate on known systems
buildSteps.detail: Check small molecules and Hubbard-type lattices against exact diagonalisation, density-matrix renormalisation group and classical diffusion Monte Carlo before trusting any new prediction.

buildSteps.title: Scale the implementation
buildSteps.detail: Grow the active space while cutting circuit depth, then move from error mitigation to error-corrected logical qubits so deep projector sequences stay coherent.

prerequisites.why: the deep, repeated projector circuits need logical error rates far below physical ones; only small logical qubits have been demonstrated.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap block encodings of fermionic Hamiltonians
prerequisites.why: circuit depth and qubit count are dominated by how the Hamiltonian is encoded, not by the Monte Carlo logic itself.
the whole method depends on a preparable state with enough overlap with the true ground state.

prerequisites.tech: Classical quantum Monte Carlo and high-performance computing
prerequisites.why: supplies the loop, the benchmarks and the strongly correlated test cases the quantum version must beat.
lets near-term devices run the sampling layer usefully before fault tolerance arrives.

pathway.milestone: small hybrid demonstrations: a superconducting processor samples a trial state and a classical auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo run is corrected by those samples (published in 2022 for a small strongly correlated system)
pathway.unlocks: evidence that quantum sampling can relieve the fermionic sign problem.

pathway.milestone: error-mitigated hybrid runs on tens of qubits for modest molecules and Fermi-Hubbard lattices
pathway.unlocks: benchmarks where classical quantum Monte Carlo is unreliable or only marginally affordable.

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant machines with enough logical qubits for deep qubitised projectors
pathway.unlocks: accurate energies for transition-metal complexes, where resource estimates for catalysts such as the FeMoco cluster of nitrogenase have long been the target.

pathway.milestone: routine quantum Monte Carlo for strongly correlated materials and catalysts
pathway.unlocks: predictive design of batteries, magnets and superconductors where classical simulation fails.
